 PIMA COUNTY, Ariz. (KVOA) -- Claims of mail ballot delays in Southern Arizona are unfounded, according to local election officials.
 The Pima County Recorder's Office announced that while nearly 480,000 ballots were mailed on Wednesday, Oct. 7, a federal holiday and common voter registration errors are causing some delivery confusion.
 Officials say some residents may have received their ballots a day or two later than expected because of the federal holiday on Monday, Oct. 12. Despite claims, the office has not observed an unusual increase in calls or messages from voters who have not received their ballots.
 Instead, election workers fielded more than 1,000 voter calls on Monday, Oct. 19, with the majority of inquiries coming from people who had recently moved. Officials note that election mail cannot be forwarded. Temporary forwarding orders through the U.S. Postal Service will result in official election mail being returned to the county.
 Other voters may not be signed up on the Active Early Voting List. Officials say a previous vote-by-mail election for the Pima County Regional Transportation Authority may have confused some voters into believing they are permanently registered to receive mail ballots.
 Voters who have not received an expected ballot can check their status online or call the county office at 520-724-4330. The deadline to make a one-time request for a mail ballot is Friday, Oct. 23.
